metals.JSL: Specialty steel and fabricated steel products

retail.LULU: Brand owners selling direct and wholesale

pharma.Export generic formulation makers: Margins depend on the number of competitors per product, the scale of first-to-market launches and regulatory inspection outcomes. Heavy buyer concentration in the US limits pricing power.

telecom.Enterprise connectivity and messaging: These companies sell managed connectivity, international capacity and messaging platforms to businesses. They earn from contracts and traffic volumes. Margin depends on competition, value-added services and the cost of buying capacity from carriers.

retail.Off-price and dollar stores: Margin depends on opportunistic buying from brands, low store costs and, for dollar stores, shipping and labor costs and exposure to lower-income customers.

semis.Foundry and memory manufacturing: These companies run fabs producing logic for others or their own DRAM and NAND. They earn from wafer or chip sales. Margins are set by process leadership and utilization, and the heavy capital spending makes memory especially cyclical.

metals.Specialty steel and fabricated steel pro: These companies make stainless steel, pipes and tubes by processing steel inputs for construction and energy customers. Margins depend on value-added mix and brand more than ore ownership. They buy steel from others, so input price swings matter.
